drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's 'mitzva group' imply liability with non-idlers?

segments.he: וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן: אָכַל בַּחֲבוּרַת מִצְוָה – אֵינוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה. טַעְמָא דְּמִצְוָה, הָא לָאו מִצְוָה – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו כּוּלָּהּ סְרִיקִין? הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּכוּלָּהּ סְרִיקִין, כֵּיוָן דִּבְמִצְוָה קָא עָסֵיק – לָא מִימְּשִׁיךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But didn’t we learn» in the mishna: If the son «ate» and drank the requisite amounts of meat and wine «with a group» assembled for the performance «of a mitzva he does not become» liable as «a stubborn and rebellious son?» A precise reading of the mishna indicates that «the reason» that he does not become liable is that he ate and drank with a group assembled for the performance «of a mitzva. But» if they were «not» assembled for the performance of «a mitzva» he would be liable «even if» the group «is not entirely» made up of «idlers.» The Gemara answers: There is no contradiction between the mishna and the statement of Rabbi Abbahu. In fact, the son is liable only if he eats with a group of whom all are idlers. And the mishna «teaches us this: That even if» the group «is entirely» composed of «idlers, since they are occupied with a mitzva,» there is «no» concern that he «will be drawn» to sin.
